Subject: Production impact: repeated tail-latency spikes (requesting credit + temporary SLA relief)

Hi Logan / Marissa,

We ran into a series of tail-latency spikes last week that caused several internal worker queues to back up and led to increased error rates in our user-facing feature. Our SREs tracked it to an intermittent model-serving stall between 11/30 and 12/03 — attached is our observed timeline (zephyr-observed-latency.csv) and sample traces.

We appreciate Redwood's responsiveness in the postmortem, but Zephyr is requesting two things while we stabilize ingest and request patterns:
- A one-month credit equivalent to our average monthly token spend to offset operational costs while we mitigate.
- A temporary "latency forgiveness" window (one month) so those spikes don't trigger our automatic remediation/penalty clauses in the contract while both sides work through root cause.

Can you confirm whether these are things Redwood can make happen? If needed, Linda (cc) is empowered to sign off on a letter of agreement quickly.

Thanks,
Alex Novak
Director of Platform Engineering
Zephyr Systems

Hi team — attached is a short summary I pulled from our telemetry (latency_summary_from_prod.pdf). Key points:
- The tail-latency spike correlates with a burst of long-context batch requests on 11/30 and a second, smaller spike on 12/02. 95th- and 99th-percentile latencies both show an elevated tail.
- Estimated customer impact window: ~36 hours total across the two incidents.
- Zephyr's monthly spend: ~$92k (last 30d tokens + embeddings).

Proposal (ops + commercial):
1) Offer a custom credit equal to 25% of Zephyr's monthly spend for the month following agreement (credit schedule in proposed_credit_schedule.xlsx).
2) Provide a 30-day "latency forgiveness" carve-out that prevents automatic penalty triggers while we (1) deploy a hotfix to request shaping and (2) roll a runtime kernel that reduces tail events for that model family.
3) Short-term operational support: 2 dedicated SRE hours/week for four weeks (no charge).

This is a conservative package that keeps costs contained while giving Zephyr immediate relief. If Finance/Exec wants a different band (50% or a full month), call it out and I’ll model cost delta.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — the summary helps. Zephyr is comfortable with the package in principle but here are two asks before Linda signs anything:
- Can Redwood make the credit 40% of monthly spend instead of 25%? That would more directly offset our remediation costs.
- We need a firm timeline on the hotfix deployment and the kernel rollout; if that slips beyond Dec 31 we’ll ask for an extension to the forgiveness window.

If Redwood can get an exec confirmation for the 40% band, Linda will sign the DocuSign we can generate. Otherwise we can proceed with the 25% proposal.

—Alex

- Limited scope: impact window ~36 hours; 40% credit is a one-off, not a precedent for larger accounts without exec signoff.
- Timeboxed: subject to a signed LOA and the timeline commitments above; we tie payment to the DocuSign link and require a small clause limiting similar claims for the same incident window.

If you approve, we’ll issue DocuSign for Linda to sign and implement the credit in billing. If you want a compromise (30–35%), call it out and we’ll negotiate quickly.
